name: Accent Hold
description:
Hold a letter (e, a, c, o, n…) and pick its accented variant (é è ê ë, ç, ñ, ô…) from a popup, with its number, the arrows or the mouse; a quick tap types the letter as usual. Works on any keyboard layout, without a daemon or root, in applications that use the GNOME input method (Wayland: GTK, VTE terminals, Electron with its Wayland backend). A shortcut (Super+E by default) opens the same picker without holding, and also works in the other applications (XWayland, Qt 5): there the chosen character is pasted through the clipboard, whose previous content is put back right after.

How a variant is picked is up to you. By default the variants stay open after you let go of the letter and Enter, a number or a click picks one, as on macOS. An option in the preferences makes releasing the letter pick the highlighted variant instead, as in PowerToys Quick Accent.

Preferences: press-and-hold on/off and duration, pick on release, shortcut, character table, keyboard layouts, optional top bar icon.
